input_origins.QueryTypedExistingLiteral: Query String parse action produces plain Literal, then algebra datatype override parses cache and keeps original decoded lexical; do not normalize again.
input_origins.QueryNumericToken: Unsigned numeric token directly constructs typed Literal from source string; normalize according to explicit source parameter. Signed tokens are separately gated by QN26.

input_origins.KnownCached: An explicitly controlled already-constructed Literal carries its original RDF identity and cache; pass it without datatype re-construction.
input_origins.UnknownNormalized: Only normalized RDF identity is available; do not infer numeric cache from lexical or global map.

receiving_protocol: Parse each listed query using the actual explicit private parser entry; lower via the existing production GraphPattern conversion with whole optimizer disabled; compile through the actual evaluator and consume real query results. Do not rebuild a replacement AST to fit expected values.

Attach the exact constructor origin before expression Literal conversion, VALUES internalization, initial preparation, and aggregate literal fast paths can discard it. QueryTypedExistingLiteral must retain decoded lexical; QueryNumericToken and DirectString follow their own actual source branches. Existing spargebra Literal AST alone may not distinguish these origins: private parser metadata is required unless a concrete distinction can be proved without guessing.

RDF expected objects assert lexical, datatype and kind exactly. Rows compare as multisets unless source input scheduling is separately asserted. Do not collapse lexical distinctions by numeric equality.

Check specified internal cache tuples at actual boundaries using crate-private receiving hooks/test access; final SELECT RDF bytes do not prove metadata survived. SELECT does not publicly serialize cache.

Explicit initial cache fixtures must use a controlled literal constructor with declared provenance; field stuffing arbitrary metadata is not sufficient. Unknown uses real normalized-only input, never silently parsed Known.
COUNT DISTINCT error instrumentation wraps the existing compiled raw evaluation callback; it does not replace evaluation with precomputed failures or fresh fake values.

Fatal cases require first Err, then None with no additional source/Dataset reads and no partial aggregate row. Dataset error identity requires actual downcast and pointer/token identity. Original Python exception propagation and Rust iterator fusion are separately classified.
Known numeric input and results must be genuine RDF literals, without invented datatype, sentinel literal, hidden global RDF-to-cache map, or second Dataset.
Run default legacy controls independently from private mode. Test implementation plus source hashes/receipts belong to a later acceptance record; this frozen file records no candidate pass.
unsupported_reporting: QN24 verifies an explicit unsupported refusal only. QN26 source parse rejection remains a named compatibility boundary until parser preparation implements it. Do not count these as successful float arithmetic or a general signed-token qualification.
